epic.label: Epic
epic.indexIntro: The great story-worlds told in order: their people and families, journeys, battles and kingdoms, each linked to the passages that tell them.
epic.storyNote: This is the story as the text tells it. Places named in it may be real; that does not make the events historical.
epic.familyNote: {count} people, each shown under the parent the text names (the legal father first). Divine, biological or foster parents, and other accounts’ versions, are noted beside them.
epic.traceLink: Trace how any two of them are connected →
epic.openBattle: Open the battlefield, day by day →
epic.politicsNote: Kingdoms of the story and the alliances, marriages and wars the text records between them. These are legendary kingdoms; historical states of the same name are separate records.

route.literary: A literary reconstruction from the text, stage by stage — not a verified itinerary. Each stop’s own page shows how confident its identification is.
route.unmapped: {count} stops have no agreed location and are not drawn on the map.

battle.literary: The battle as the epic tells it: formations, encounters and deaths are literary, not an archaeological or historical record.
battle.sideNote: Sides: {a} and {b}. The table lists everyone the text says fell, in order of days.
